chunks: One of them is Amr bin Lohi, whose real name was Rabia bin Haritha bin Amr Maziqiya. According to scholars of Khaza,

he was the chief of the Khaza during the battle between Khaza and Jurham. He had initiated the customs of Saiba, Wasila and Haam. He brought the idols of Hubal and Manat from Syria to Mecca. He entrusted Hubal to Khazima bin Mudrika and that is why it began to be referred to as the Hubal Khazima. Then he placed Manat on Mt. Abu Qubais and he was the first to bring Nard (a dice game) to Mecca, which people played all the time in Kaaba and its vicinity.

key_terms.السَّائِبَة: Sa'iba, a custom of freeing camels for idol worship
key_terms.الْحَام: Haam, a custom of freeing a male camel
key_terms.الْوَصِيلَة: Wasila, a custom of freeing a female camel
key_terms.عَمْرُو بْنُ لَحْيٍ: Amr bin Lohi, a pre-Islamic Arab leader

ai.seo_question: Who was Amr bin Lohi and what were his contributions to pre-Islamic Arabian religious practices?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi highlights Amr bin Lohi as a key architect of pre-Islamic religious deviation, credited with institutionalizing the 'Sawiba' and 'Wasila' customs and introducing idolatry to Mecca by bringing Hubble and Manat from Syria. His role in placing these idols at specific sites like Abu Qubais and Al-Musalla underscores the geographical and spiritual corruption that preceded the Prophet's mission. This account serves as a historical precursor to the Quranic critique of Jahiliyyah practices, illustrating the transition from monotheism to polytheism in the Arabian Peninsula.
